spec.description: OHLC candles for one product over a time range, newest first. Each candle is a fixed six-column row rather than an object.

request.title: GetCandlesRequest
request.description: Which product, over which span, at which resolution.

product_id.description: Product id, such as `BTC-USD`. `products.list_products` returns it as `id`.

granularity.description: Bucket width in seconds: one minute, five, fifteen, one hour, six hours, one day. Any other value is rejected.

response.title: Candles
response.description: The candles in the span, newest first.

notes: Both bounds are inclusive, so the step is one second: a window whose `end` equalled the previous window's `start` would re-read the candle on the boundary. Confirmed against the live API -- `start=00:00Z&end=05:00Z` at hourly granularity returns six candles, not five.

No `size` is declared, and so no truncation guard is generated, because the endpoint has no page-size parameter to declare. The exchange caps a response at 300 candles and says nothing about the ones it withheld, which is exactly the loss the guard exists to catch; `pagination.size` can only name a request parameter, and there is none here. See the registry README's note on this spec.
